Outline of logic
Logic
is the
formal science
of using
reason
and is considered a branch of both
philosophy
and
mathematics
and to a lesser extent
computer science
. Logic investigates and classifies the structure of statements and arguments, both through the study of
formal systems
of inference and the study of arguments in
natural language
. The scope of logic can therefore be very large, ranging from core topics such as the study of
fallacies
and
paradoxes
, to specialized analyses of reasoning such as
probability
, correct reasoning, and arguments involving
causality
. One of the aims of logic is to identify the correct (or
valid
) and incorrect (or
fallacious
)
inferences
. Logicians study the criteria for the evaluation of
arguments
.

Computability theory
–
branch of mathematical logic that originated in the 1930s with the study of computable functions and
Turing degrees
. The field has grown to include the study of generalized computability and definability. The basic questions addressed by recursion theory are "What does it mean for a function from the natural numbers to themselves to be computable?" and "How can noncomputable functions be classified into a hierarchy based on their level of noncomputability?". The answers to these questions have led to a rich theory that is still being actively researched.
